title: Roasting Temperature and Particle Size Govern Gold Release and Desulfurization of a Historical Peruvian Pyritic Tailing
content: Tailings containing pyrite generate acid drainage and still contain gold that direct cyanidation fails to recover. The Santa Catalina tailings (Peru), containing 2.4 g/t Au, 62 g/t Ag, and about 60% pyrite, were studied. Although more than 99% of the pyrite was liberated, direct cyanidation extracted only 13–14% of the gold. The tailings were roasted at temperatures between 400 and 800 °C using two particle sizes, and the calcines were cyanidated. Scanning electron microscopy revealed 2 µm gold particles and silver tellurides containing gold in the pyrite of the calcines at 400–500 °C. The pyrite transformed into porous hematite from the edge toward the center, passing through pyrrhotite. Grinding to 95% −38 µm lowered the temperature required for sulfur removal by about 100 °C compared to 60% −75 µm. The optimal condition—600 °C with fine grinding—extracted 52.7% of the gold and 37.7% of the silver. At 800 °C, gold extraction dropped to 25–27%, likely due to the formation of Zn and Cu ferrites. Temperature accounted for 68% of the variation in gold extraction. To scale up the process, it is advisable to first concentrate the pyrite by flotation and to reduce the high cyanide consumption caused by copper.
